assumptions: The converged specification and accepted SDD-001 invariants are authoritative despite remaining DRAFT labels.
The blockers concern implementation structure and enforcement of settled requirements; they do not reopen Spec Grill policy.
Provider-modified repository code executed by verification is within the stated untrusted-worktree threat model; this is distinct from a hostile local OS owner.
This was static architecture review. No tests, providers, verification commands or prototypes were executed, and no files or external systems were modified.
blocking_questions: AG-01 — Where is verification authority protected across every entry point? Plan §§5–6 place authoritative evidence under .agent-runs/verification/ and reuse the existing sandbox. However, verification_sandbox.py:82–126 grants writes throughout the execution worktree. Counterexample: direct CLI verification executes in the control checkout; a provider-modified build script can then overwrite evidence or remove failure fences inside that writable checkout. The command allowlist does not prevent writes performed by an allowed script, and receipt hashes are not authentication. Checkout-relative stores also permit separate authority/lock namespaces when invoked from linked worktrees. Smallest design change: define one canonical repository/control-store resolver shared by all entry points, and an execution boundary that prevents child processes from modifying authoritative evidence, policy, locks and authorization records. Specify how each sandbox backend and degraded/off mode preserves that boundary; directory separation alone is insufficient when the child remains unrestricted.

AG-02 — How does failure-specific authorization compose with task-level human-resolve? Plan §8 requires one-shot authorization but defines neither its owner nor its consumption transaction. Existing harness.py:924–942 consumes a task-level grant before provider execution; cmd_human_resolve at :1183 requires an escalated DAG task. Counterexample: a direct integration gate fails without any DAG task, so existing human-resolve cannot authorize it. For a task-bound failure, interpreting the generic task grant as verification permission can authorize the wrong failure; consuming only a derived fence/index entry allows replay after reconstruction. Smallest design change: extend the existing audited human-resolution mechanism with an explicit verification-failure scope and a durable, failure-bound consumption record. Define consumption before process launch, crash recovery, task-grant versus gate-grant ownership, and lock ordering. Preserve each failed terminal attempt, and map fenced verification outcomes through runner/orchestrator without automatically relaunching the builder as ordinary rework.

AG-03 — When are consumer fingerprints and reuse decisions finalized? Plan §§1, 6–7 describe a precomputed plan, followed by execution and post-execution recomputation, but do not define dependency rebinding before a gate executes or reuses evidence. Counterexample: producer P must regenerate a missing artifact; consumer C's planned fingerprint references P's old receipt. After P runs, C must reference the new receipt and current artifact bytes. Executing C with the old pre-fingerprint creates false stale-input; retaining its earlier REUSE decision can accept stale producer identity. A later focused test can similarly overwrite an artifact after the initial plan. Smallest design change: distinguish the plan snapshot from authoritative ready-gate evaluation. Under repository ownership, the shared engine must resolve current dependency receipts/artifacts, finalize the pre-fingerprint and revalidate RUN/REUSE immediately before each gate. Wrappers must consume those structured decisions without implementing their own replanning algorithm.

findings: Q1 / SDD-001 compatibility: Yes, the feature is implementable without changing accepted freshness semantics. Full task-command dependency closure and distinct duplicate occurrences can use the same engine as integration, with mandatory freshness expressed as planner policy. Unmapped legacy commands remain fresh and non-cacheable.

Q2 / Module boundaries: Prefer a thin verify.py CLI over a small verification package separating policy/input fingerprinting, planning, evidence/ownership, and execution. Reporting should remain in telemetry.py. This is a non-blocking organization recommendation; one file is not inherently unsafe. Extract the existing allowlist/execution bridge into a neutral dependency, or inject it, so runner importing verification does not require verification to import runner.

Q3 / Profile schema: The proposed fields are appropriately bounded for the accepted contract. Use closed, versioned structures for probes and retry controls, with concrete cwd and artifact-root identities. Do not introduce arbitrary shell probes, expression evaluation or a scripting DSL. Expensive/category/description metadata must not silently acquire gate-selection authority.

Q4 / Evidence authority: Terminal evidence plus a rebuildable index can avoid split brain, provided AG-01 and AG-02 are resolved. Index entries and summary.json must remain projections, never independent PASS or retry authorization. Reconstruction must validate terminal schema, ownership, receipt integrity and dependency references. Failure and grant-consumption history must survive index deletion.

Q5 / Locking: Repository-wide serialization is sufficient for the accepted single-machine, single-writer model. Its placement is not yet fully established: all worktrees/profiles need the same canonical ownership namespace, acquired before authoritative decision validation and retained through execution, terminal publication and index update. Planning outside that lock is advisory. The current per-feature task lock is not a substitute.

Q6 / Human resolution: Reuse the existing audit and one-shot authorization concepts, but not the current generic grant counter unchanged. Direct verification has no mandatory task, and gate authorization binds to a particular failure/fingerprint. AG-02 is required to avoid duplicate or replayable authorization systems.

Q7 / Telemetry extension: The design can remain an extension of telemetry.py. Provider provenance owns invocation metadata; verification terminal receipts own gate execution facts; reports join them by trusted identifiers. Do not copy independently mutable gate outcomes into a second telemetry store. Preserve legacy aggregate reporting while incomplete ordering produces UNKNOWN.

Q8 / Runtime choice: There is no reason to introduce a general orchestration framework. None of the blockers requires distributed scheduling or a workflow database; another persistence model would complicate evidence and authorization ownership.

Q9 / Prototype: No prototype is currently justified. The blockers require explicit architecture decisions and deterministic adversarial tests, not an empirical technology selection. Backend protection and crash behavior should be verified during implementation.

Q10 / Required pre-implementation changes: Amend the plan with the protected canonical control-store/execution boundary, the failure-scoped authorization transaction and lifecycle mapping, and ready-gate dependency/fingerprint finalization. Include harness.py and verification_sandbox.py as explicit implementation dependencies where those decisions require changes. Then obtain a fresh Architecture Grill before the hash-bound design gate and independent verification contract.

Fingerprinting: Use batched Git primitives for ancestry, committed changes and dirty/untracked overlays, with NUL-delimited paths and rename detection disabled for changed-surface construction. Retain the specified mini-glob rather than substituting host glob or fnmatch semantics. Non-following component inspection must cover ancestors as well as final path objects. Tool probes need bounded execution and allowlisted output formats; they must not become a second command-authorization path.

Artifacts: Generic produces/consumes declarations, contained roots, exact producer receipts and byte manifests are sufficient; no JaCoCo-specific engine logic is needed. Validate source/artifact overlap across the selected family and enforce the AG-03 timing boundary. A non-cacheable producer must not indirectly authorize consumer reuse.

Manual evidence: Registration remains observability only. Parse canonical markers with an explicit Markdown block-state parser rather than a global regex; validate symlink ancestors, commit binding and conflicting identities. Completed at is an asserted review timestamp whose eligibility comes from trusted scope and chronological checks, not proof of task completion.

Privacy: A shared allowlisted serializer should validate nested metadata, safe paths, probe outputs, numeric usage and diagnostic enums before persistence and report rendering. Redaction must never supply fingerprint identity. Extend canary coverage to all channels listed in the specification, beyond the three examples retained in plan §13.

Performance: The 100-gate/5,000-file benchmark is reasonable as a regression alarm. Compile matchers once per validated profile, batch Git inspection and deduplicate file hashing within a snapshot. Do not reuse cached content hashes across the required post-execution observation merely because size or timestamps match.

Compatibility: Legacy verification arrays can enter the shared engine through synthetic occurrence nodes without requiring profile migration. Read v1 provenance without rewriting it; unsupported records cannot authorize reuse. Current orchestration state is protocol-fingerprint-bound and already refuses drift, so document deliberate upgrade/replanning rather than promising transparent mid-run migration. Keep v2 verification data in the separate subtree older harness versions ignore.

Documentation: Keep handbook.md authoritative and generate the PDF from it through one documented build path. Maintain concise README workflow summaries and commands checked against the same canonical examples. Validate required content and visually inspect the rendered PDF; binary byte equality is not the source-of-truth test.
non_blocking_risks: Lock lifetime must cover active command descendants, not just the Python parent. A killed executor or expired task lease must not release verification ownership while a child still writes artifacts. Test this separately from ordinary terminal-record crash recovery.

Give every continuation a distinct verification-attempt identity and immutable terminal paths. Reusing runs/<id>/gates/<gate-id>.json for successive attempts would overwrite failure history. Encode occurrence identifiers safely instead of using unrestricted logical ids as filenames.

Preserve runner.py's existing whole-worktree mutation postcondition independently of selective reuse fingerprints. Replacing it with declared-input checking alone would weaken existing protection against verification commands modifying unmatched source files.

Persist trusted invocation identity separately from immutable task packets. Current runner provenance takes role from packet.role even for specialist overrides, and packets contain no task-attempt number. Role, task attempt, lineage and required-review scope must come from control-plane dispatch/state, not provider claims or directory-name inference.

Define runner/orchestrator handling of busy, stale-input and environment-blocked explicitly. The current boolean verification result and generic fail path lose these distinctions and can consume rework attempts or relaunch providers unnecessarily.

Centralize safe serialization. Current telemetry parsers retain arbitrary provider usage dictionaries; runner provenance retains command strings, provider-reported paths and exception messages. Extending those dictionaries directly would violate the v2 field policy.
Keep eval.py output hashes/tails diagnostic and outside reusable GREEN authority. Its current result records cannot be imported wholesale into secret-minimized v2 evidence.
residual_risks: Profile completeness remains an independent authoring/evaluation obligation; fingerprints cannot detect omitted result-sensitive inputs.
Hostile local OS modification and transient external A-to-B-to-A writes remain outside the accepted guarantee.
Sandbox enforcement, process-lifetime locking, crash publication and grant consumption require implementation evidence.
Architecture PASS, a current hash-bound design gate and an accepted independent verification contract remain required before executable task generation.
summary: The accepted specification is implementable without changing SDD-001 semantics, but three architecture decisions need resolution before implementation: protection of verification authority, failure-specific human authorization, and execution-time dependency binding. No framework migration or prototype is justified. This review was read-only.
